chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

The palm tree of Maryam (peace be upon her) was Al-Ajwa, and it was sent down in the month of Kanun (December/January), and Al-Ateeq and Al-Ajwa were sent down with Adam (peace be upon him), and from it the varieties of palm trees disseminated.

key_terms.آدَمَ: Adam (peace be upon him), the first human and prophet
key_terms.الْعَتِيقُ: Al-Ateeq, another specific variety of dates mentioned in this context
key_terms.الْعَجْوَةُ: Al-Ajwa, a specific and highly regarded variety of dates
key_terms.كَانُونَ: Kanun, a month in the lunar calendar (often corresponding to December/January)
key_terms.نَخْلَةُ مَرْيَمَ: The palm tree of Maryam (mother of Prophet Isa)

ai.seo_question: What is the origin and significance of Al-Ajwa and Al-Ateeq dates according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi traces the botanical and spiritual lineage of dates, identifying Al-Ajwa as the specific variety belonging to Maryam (peace be upon her) and Al-Ateeq as the original date sent down with Adam (peace be upon him). It highlights the theological significance of these fruits as divine provisions, linking the purity associated with Maryam to the primordial bounty granted to humanity, thereby establishing a sacred history for one of the most revered foods in Islamic tradition.
